title: Completed conormal presentations and normalized comparison data
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $S$ a commutative $k$-algebra, and $A$ a commutative local $S$-algebra with the compatible $k$-algebra structure. Put $R=\widehat A$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak m_A R$, and $N=R\otimes_A\Omega^1_{A/k}$ [def-trf-completed-jacobian-presentation], using Kähler differentials [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] and scalar extension [def-weil-module-base-change]. Fix $d\geq0$ and a supplied adjunction system $\mathcal J$ for $\operatorname{Spec}S\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-sfb-flat-lci-adjunction-system]. The following are definitions of data and normalization conditions, with no assertion that such data exist.

An algebraic presentation consists of $m\geq d$, a rational maximal ideal $\mathfrak q\subset k[u_1,\ldots,u_m]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], a surjective $k$-algebra map $P=k[u]_{\mathfrak q}\to A$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], and a specified regular sequence of $m-d$ elements generating its kernel $I$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. A formal presentation consists of $n,c$ with $c+d=n$, a continuous local surjection $T=k[[z_1,\ldots,z_n]]\to R$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series] for the variable-adic and $\mathfrak n$-adic topologies, and a specified regular sequence $g_1,\ldots,g_c$ in the variable ideal generating its kernel $J$.

A two-term conormal model retains its actual modules $E^{-1},E^0$, differential and ranks $a,b$. Its complex is in degrees $-1,0$, and its associated sheaf complex is on $\operatorname{Spec}R$, with derived category [def-pc-derived-category]. Its line is $(\bigwedge^a E^{-1})^\vee\otimes\bigwedge^b E^0$, using exterior powers [def-weil-pbc-exterior-algebra], their sheaf versions [def-sc-sheaf-exterior-power], and dual $\mathcal Hom(-,\mathcal O)$. The algebraic model is $[R\otimes_A I/I^2\to R\otimes_A( A\otimes_P\Omega^1_{P/k})]$ with its universal differential; its augmentation to $N$ is the scalar extension of the universal cokernel map. The formal model is $[J/J^2\xrightarrow{\delta}R^n]$. Formal differential data for a specified $D:R\to N$ consist of $\delta$, an augmentation $q:R^n\to N$, and a basis $b_j$ of the actual conormal quotient, with $b_j=[g_j]$, $\delta([h])=(\pi(\partial_i h))_i$ for every $h\in J$, $q(e_i)=D(\pi(z_i))$, and the injectivity, exactness and surjectivity of this sequence. Formal partial derivatives are [def-trf-formal-power-series-partial-derivative]. The canonical section of an associated module sheaf is the image of its module element under the affine tilde/global-sections equivalence.

A map of two-term models retains the actual two linear maps and the induced chain map. Its determinant predicate is the exact-cone normalization of [def-sfb-flat-lci-adjunction-system]. An algebraic-to-formal lift is a local $k$-algebra map $\alpha:P\to T$ with $\pi\alpha$ equal to $P\to A\to R$. Its induced map must send $[h]\otimes1$ to $[\alpha(h)]$, and $\mathrm du\otimes1$ to the vector of formal derivatives of $\alpha(u)$. Algebraic presentation changes similarly act on ideal classes and universal differentials. A continuous formal presentation change is an ambient continuous $k$-algebra map over $1_R$; its conormal map sends $[h]$ to the class of its image and its degree-zero map sends $e_i$ to the formal derivative vector of the image of $z_i$. Chain maps also determine their associated-sheaf maps and, when quasi-isomorphisms, the actual derived isomorphisms.

The affine adjunction sections are the global sections of $\mathcal J$ at the identity base change [def-sfb-flat-lci-base-change]. Their scalar extension to $R$ is the completed source line. A field-valued point is generic-smooth if the kernel of $A\to L$ is a minimal prime and $\operatorname{Spec}L\to\operatorname{Spec}S$ factors through a smooth open [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. The algebraic smooth-comparison predicate on a map from adjunction sections to $\bigwedge^d_L(L\otimes_A\Omega^1_{A/k})$ requires an affine smooth presentation neighbourhood, its relation-first normalized adjunction comparison to top differentials, and the induced evaluation map on differential wedges. The evaluating derivation satisfies Leibniz and sends every restricted $s\in S$ to $1\otimes\mathrm d(s|_A)$; the wedge evaluation sends $a\,\mathrm db_1\wedge\cdots\wedge\mathrm db_d$ to the value of $a$ times the wedge of those evaluated differentials. The supplied map must equal this composite on every adjunction section.

For a formal presentation and field $L$, the generic Jacobian has columns $(\theta\pi(\partial_i g_j))_i$ and the generic augmentation sends $e_i$ to $D(\pi(z_i))\otimes1$. The generic determinant predicate on $\Delta:\bigwedge^d_L(L\otimes_A\Omega^1_{A/k})\simeq L\otimes_R\lambda_T$ requires, for every dual conormal section evaluating to $1$ on $[g_1]\wedge\cdots\wedge[g_c]$, every tuple $v_i$ and every tuple of lifts $\widetilde v_i$ under the generic augmentation, the relation-first formula $\Delta(v_1\wedge\cdots\wedge v_d)=([g_1]\wedge\cdots\wedge[g_c])^\vee\otimes(\widehat{\mathrm d}g_1\wedge\cdots\wedge\widehat{\mathrm d}g_c\wedge\widetilde v_1\wedge\cdots\wedge\widetilde v_d)$, expressed by its coefficient determinant in the standard coordinate basis.

A completed conormal determinant comparison system consists of: a derivation $D$ satisfying the continuous-extension predicate [def-trf-completed-differential-extension]; formal differential data for every formal presentation; isomorphisms from the completed source to every formal and algebraic determinant line; exactness and the equation/coordinate ranks of every algebraic model; local lifts and their actual quasi-isomorphic chain maps whose augmentations commute and whose determinants identify the source comparisons; equality of the derived classes for all lifts; and the analogous normalized algebraic and continuous formal presentation-change maps. For each generic-smooth field it additionally supplies one algebraic smooth-comparison isomorphism $\gamma$, and for every formal presentation the short exact generic conormal sequence and a determinant isomorphism $\Delta$ satisfying the preceding predicate and $\Delta\gamma=\Phi_T\otimes_R L$ on all adjunction sections. The comparison between two formal determinant lines is defined as $\Phi_U\Phi_T^{-1}$, through their common source. Empty relation lists, empty wedges, $d=0$, and zero ranks use the same definitions. This structure is a type of supplied systems, not its inhabitation theorem.
